Veridrop publishes its prices for common tests

REDMONT, Ore. (July 2, 2015) — Veridrop today published the price of every test it offers, so that a patient can see the cost before a sample is taken.

Under the new list a cholesterol panel costs $9.65, a complete blood count costs $5.35 and an HSV-1 test costs $9.07 at every Veridrop collection room.

The company said the prices apply to patients with and without insurance, and that no separate fee is charged for collecting the sample.

Veridrop operates collection rooms in 41 pharmacy stores in Oregon and Nevada, and said it plans to open more over the next two years.

"A person should know what a test costs before agreeing to it," said Dana Marlowe, the company's founder and chief executive.

The list covers more than 200 tests and will be reviewed twice a year. Changes will be dated and the earlier price will stay visible for ninety days.

A technician warms the patient's hand, presses a small device against a fingertip and seals the sample before it is sent by courier to the central Veridrop laboratory.

Veridrop collection sites are small rooms beside a pharmacy counter, with a chair, a refrigerator and a screen that tells a visitor how long the visit is likely to take.

Doctors who have sent patients to the collection rooms said the reports arrived quickly and were laid out clearly, with earlier results printed alongside the new ones.

Insurers have been slow to say what they think. Two regional plans confirmed that they pay for the company's tests under existing billing codes, and a third declined to comment.

For now Veridrop depends on a handful of agreements, the largest with a pharmacy chain that is still deciding how many of its stores will get a collection room.

State rules differ on who may order a blood test, and Veridrop has spent part of its money asking legislatures to change those rules.

About Veridrop

Veridrop is a privately held laboratory company founded in 2008 and based in Redmont, Oregon. It employs about 500 people.
